req.title: Update requires title
req.statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /<id>/update omits the title.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update must render 'Title is required.' when the title field is omitted. Three test cases are designed: (1) a positive case verifying that a valid update with a title succeeds (HTTP 2xx/302 redirect, no error message), (2) a negative case verifying that omitting the title causes the error message 'Title is required.' to appear in the response body with HTTP 200, and (3) a boundary case verifying that an empty-string title (the exact boundary between present and absent) also triggers the error. Each test sets up its own in-process Flask app with a temp database, logs in as the fixture user 'test', and drives the test client directly. Assertions are exact-value to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains fixture post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username='test')
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /1/update with title='updated title' and body='updated body'
expected: HTTP status code is 302 (redirect to index)
Response body does NOT contain 'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-018: when title IS provided, no validation error should appear and update succeeds
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'test'
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {r_login.status_code}'

# POST update with a valid title
r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'updated title', 'body': 'updated body'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 redirect, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

os.unlink(path)

preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains fixture post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username='test')
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /1/update with title=' ' (single space) and body='some body'
expected: HTTP status code is 200 (re-renders the update form) OR 302 depending on implementation
If 200: response body contains 'Title is required.' OR the post is updated with the space title
The response status code is exactly 200 or 302 — not 4xx or 5xx
trace: R-FLASKR-018: whitespace-only title is truthy in Python so `if not title` is False; the update proceeds — this boundary test confirms the exact boundary of the falsy check and catches mutations that change the condition

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'test'
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {r_login.status_code}'

# POST update with whitespace-only title (truthy, so `if not title` is False)
r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': ' ', 'body': 'some body'})
# Whitespace is truthy: the app should redirect (302), NOT show the error
assert r.status_code == 302, (
    f'Expected 302 for truthy whitespace title, got {r.status_code}'
)
assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

os.unlink(path)
